## Verdict

**Dorado** costs least for a team of 9, at **$171 per month** — despite having the highest per-seat rate on the list. It is the only vendor whose minimum (1 seat) falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly 9 seats. Inkwell's cheaper $8 seat is undercut by a 10-seat floor, and Borealis bills for 25 seats regardless.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $19 | 1 |
| Inkwell | $8 | 10 |
| Borealis | $12 | 25 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 9 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Dorado:** minimum 1 < 9, so 9 seats paid. 9 × $19 = **$171 per month**. Effective rate $19.00 per person.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 10 > 9, so 10 seats paid. 10 × $8 = **$80 per month**. Effective rate $8.89 per person ($80 ÷ 9).
- **Borealis:** minimum 25 > 9, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $12 = **$300 per month**. Effective rate $33.33 per person ($300 ÷ 9).

Correcting the verdict above: **Inkwell is cheapest at $80 per month**, not Dorado. Its 10-seat minimum costs the team one unused seat ($8), but that padding is far smaller than Dorado's rate premium. Inkwell is $91 per month cheaper than Dorado and $220 cheaper than Borealis — $1,092 and $2,640 per year respectively.

## Risks

Inkwell's one wasted seat disappears entirely at 10 people, where it costs $80 against Dorado's $190. Its lead widens with growth, since it carries both the lowest per-seat rate and a minimum the team has nearly cleared.

Borealis's $300 is a fixed floor until 25 seats. It does not become competitive against Inkwell at any size on this list, since $12 exceeds $8 per seat throughout.

Dorado's appeal is flexibility, not price: with a 1-seat minimum it never bills for unused capacity. That matters only below 10 people, and even at 9 it costs more than Inkwell's padded minimum.

This comparison covers list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, or contract terms, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, discounts, and onboarding fees are not in the source and could change the ranking.
